course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict

lesson.title: Causes of World War II
lesson.summary: How fascism, the failure of the peace settlement, appeasement, and Japanese expansion led to a second world war.
learningGoals: Explain the causes and consequences of World War II.
lesson.bigIdea: Fascist expansion, Japanese imperialism, and the failure of other powers to stop them led to World War II.
lesson.context: The Depression and the unpopular peace settlement weakened democracies and strengthened extremists.

sections.title: The rise of fascism

blocks.text: Fascism glorified the nation, rejected democracy and communism, and demanded obedience to a single leader. Mussolini took power in Italy in 1922, and Hitler became chancellor of Germany in 1933.
Both regimes used propaganda and violence and promised national greatness through expansion. The Nazis persecuted Jews from the start.

sections.takeaway: Fascist regimes rejected democracy and pursued expansion by force.

sections.title: Appeasement and expansion

blocks.text: Britain and France tried appeasement, giving in to some demands to avoid war. At Munich in 1938 they allowed Germany to take the Sudetenland. Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939.
In Asia, Japan seized Manchuria in 1931 and invaded China in 1937. After the United States cut off oil, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Fascist and Japanese expansion went unchecked by appeasement, which encouraged further aggression until war broke out.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: World War II began in Asia before 1939. Japan's war in China started in 1937.

sections.takeaway: Unchecked aggression in Europe and Asia produced a global war.

connections.title: From Versailles to war
connections.body: Resentment of the Treaty of Versailles helped the Nazis win support, linking the end of one war to the start of the next.
connections.transferQuestion: How did the outcome of World War I contribute to World War II?
connections.feedback: Name a specific result of the first war and explain its effect.
